title.en: Soils of India and soil conservation

text.en: A farmer in the Ganga plains grows rice and wheat, while a Deccan farmer grows cotton. The difference begins beneath their feet, in the soil.

Soil is the uppermost layer of the land, made of minerals, organic matter, living organisms, air and water, formed by weathering of rocks.
The ICAR (set up in 1953) classifies Indian soils into eight groups: alluvial, black, red, laterite, forest and mountain, arid and desert, saline and alkaline, peaty and marshy.
Alluvial soil is deposited by rivers, rich in potash, phosphoric acid and lime but poor in nitrogen; it suits rice, wheat, sugarcane and oilseeds.
Black soil, from Deccan basalt, is rich in lime, iron and potash, holds moisture well and is sticky when wet, ideal for cotton.
Red soil forms from granite and gneiss and is rich in iron but deficient in nitrogen, humus and lime; it grows wheat, cotton and pulses.
Laterite soil forms by leaching in alternate wet and dry conditions; it is acidic and suits coffee, rubber, cashew and tapioca.
Forest soils are rich in humus; desert soils are sandy and saline; saline soils suffer from excess salts; peaty soils occur in humid regions with heavy rain.
Soil erosion, degradation, water-logging and salinisation are major problems; IIRS (2015) estimated 147 million hectares affected by erosion.
Conservation methods: afforestation, dams and barrages, preventing overgrazing, contour bunding, crop rotation, strip cropping, shelter belts and sustainable agriculture.

problem.en: A farmer in Maharashtra grows cotton and a farmer in Assam hills grows coffee. Which soils do they likely have and why?

text.en: Maharashtra lies on the Deccan lava plateau with black soil.
Black soil retains moisture and is rich in lime, ideal for cotton.
Assam hills have laterite soil formed by leaching under wet and dry conditions.
Laterite suits coffee, rubber, cashew and tapioca.

prompt.en: Suggest three measures to stop erosion on a hill farm.

points.en: Alluvial: plains; black: cotton; red; laterite: coffee and rubber.
Conserve by contour bunding, rotation, afforestation.
